name: Tongariro Northern Circuit
why: Over Red Crater and the Emerald Lakes, then round the foot of Ngauruhoe through lava fields and the Rangipo desert.
book: Huts and campsites must be booked all year round; Great Walk season 23 Oct-30 Apr. The Whakapapa-Mangatepopo section is closed after the 2025 fire: start at Mangatepopo car park (shuttle from National Park Village or Whakapapa). Do not climb Ngauruhoe or Tongariro summits: sacred to Ngāti Tūwharetoa.
water: Tap water at huts, untreated: boil it. None on the crater section.
dangers: Alpine weather at the craters: strong wind, cold and cloud even in summer.
Loose rock on the steep slopes of Red Crater and the descent to the Emerald Lakes.
An active volcanic area: check the volcanic alert level.
turnaround: If it is windy or in cloud at Mangatepopo Saddle, turn back to Mangatepopo: the crater section has no shelter.

points.name: Mangatepopo car park
points.note: Start of the circuit since the 2025 fire. Mangatepopo Hut is 25 min away.

points.name: Emerald Lakes
points.note: Coloured lakes in old explosion pits below Red Crater, the highest point of the walk.

points.name: Oturere Hut
points.note: First night, at the edge of the Oturere valley lava fields, below Ngauruhoe.

points.name: Waihohonu Hut
points.note: Second night, in a beech valley. The 1904 historic hut is 10 min off the track.

points.name: Whakapapa Village
points.note: After Tama Saddle and Taranaki Falls, 15.4 km from Waihohonu. Lower Tama Lake is a 20 min side trip.
